findings.creator: llm-research
findings.topic: Benchmark scores stopped being evidence about two years ago, and the field's own papers say so
findings.title: reversals[] cannot express a turn that points against the notebook's own thesis
findings.expected: A reversal schema in which at least one turn may conclude that the obvious reading survives, or a required field stating why no such turn exists.
findings.got: {obvious_reading, why_wrong, mechanism, evidence[], escalation}. The second field presupposes the obvious reading fails; escalation requires each turn to compound in the same direction. A counter-direction turn has no field and would have to be smuggled into `note`.
findings.refuter: Checked whether the reference run refutes it. r4 ('So institutional adoption failed' -> 'It succeeded completely') looks like a counter-direction reversal and is not: it reverses the reader's momentary inference and lands harder on the notebook's stated verdict (notebook.json:14), and its own note says 'This is the final turn and the thesis'. The worked reference demonstrates the bias rather than disproving it. Marked `undecided` because the content|lens axis has no value for 'the shared mechanism is wrong for every seat' — this is not a tech-specific need.
findings.l2_priority: Run the topic and count reversal directions. If all reversals point one way in a topic whose honest answer is mixed, this is confirmed at L2 with a produced artifact.

findings.creator: llm-research
findings.topic: Benchmark scores stopped being evidence about two years ago
findings.title: The mandatory research-time verdict contradicts Engine D's second honesty tell
findings.expected: Either the verdict is provisional until the candidate set is weighed, or ENGINES.md's tell 2 is qualified to say the prior is fixed by design and names what protects it.
findings.got: NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md requires `verdict` — the one-sentence answer — 'Written during research, not during scripting'. ENGINES.md D-honest tell 2 asks 'Can any candidate actually win against the author's prior? If the theories are three framings of one conclusion, the adjudication is decorative.' engine_fit is not assessed until Phase 8, after the verdict, tension, reversals and steel-man are all committed. The two files never cite each other.
findings.refuter: Is 'answer early' just correct craft? Yes — CRAFT-BASELINE.md:97-99 is right that explanatory content states the thesis at 0:40. The defect is not that a verdict exists; it is that a verdict dated to research time cannot be moved by anything a render-time candidate enumeration discovers. Would a competent execution avoid it? Only by ignoring a mandatory field.
findings.l2_priority: Record the timestamp order: was the verdict written before or after the candidate set? If before, D-rigged is confirmed as the default path.

findings.topic: Benchmark scores stopped being evidence about two years ago
findings.title: Two of three D-honest tells are unenforceable from the notebook, and the reference render self-grades its own honesty check
findings.expected: A candidates[] field the premise-challenging candidate can be asserted in, and an honesty check computed rather than declared.
findings.got: No candidates[] field exists anywhere in the schema; the candidate set is improvised at render time. Tell 1 survives in the reference run only as free prose inside an engine_fit[].why string. The rendered script carries a five-row 'Engine-D honesty check' table with green ticks written by the same pass that wrote the script — and its one computable row reads 'target >=30% — this render runs high by construction; measure before shipping', shipped unmeasured with a tick beside it. Only tell 3 has structural teeth, via the mandatory steel_man.
findings.refuter: Is this the creator's topic being hard? No — the tells are subject-independent by their own claim ('all checkable without knowing the subject', ENGINES.md:86). Is it present somewhere unread? Grepped: no candidates concept in pipeline/ or knowledge/. Is a self-graded table adequate? It is the exact appearance-of-weighing that ENGINES.md:83-85 defines as the failure mode.
findings.l2_priority: Compute causal-opener density on the produced adjudication render instead of declaring it. If the tick was correct, the finding narrows to enforceability; if not, it widens.

findings.creator: llm-research
findings.topic: Benchmark scores stopped being evidence about two years ago
findings.title: Engine C is the only non-takedown engine and the schema cannot hold its familiar domain
findings.expected: A field holding a second domain's facts, mechanism and sources, so Parallel Case is reachable as more than a one-line analogy.
findings.got: analogy_candidates[] is {for, analogy, quality}, one line per entry, with the schema noting 'Short form gets one or zero'. ENGINES.md requires the familiar half to come first, run longer, and do all the mechanical work — MinuteEarth spends 67 of 114 seconds there. There is no other field for a second domain; facts[] and mechanisms[] are about the subject. engine_fit will therefore correctly mark parallel-case 'poor — no second domain to transfer to', exactly as the reference run did, and be right about a notebook that had no way to hold one.
findings.refuter: Could the second domain live in facts[] with a tag? Yes — which is precisely the content fix, and why this is content and not lens. But nothing in the schema or prompt suggests it, and the field that appears to be for it caps the material at one line and grades it 'medium, consider dropping'. This is the finding that converts 'the methodic only produces takedowns' from a preference into a structural claim: the escape hatch exists in the engine catalogue and is welded shut by the schema.
findings.l2_priority: Attempt a Parallel Case render from the produced notebook. If it cannot be built without re-researching a second domain, confirmed.

findings.creator: llm-research
findings.topic: Benchmark scores stopped being evidence about two years ago
findings.title: confidence conflates 'the number is right' with 'the number measures what it claims'
findings.expected: A per-fact way to say: this figure is precise AND the construct it measures is disputed.
findings.got: facts[].confidence is high|medium|low. GPQA-Diamond 59.4% is reproducible to a decimal and is plausibly a measurement of a partially-memorised instrument scored on a construct its own authors hedge. `confidence: high` is correct and certifies the wrong thing. The nearest expressible form is unknowns[].impact — genuinely the best-designed field in the schema, and the right idea — but an unknown has no pointer to a fact id, so a notebook with twelve figures of which three are contested constructs cannot say which three. facts[].note would hold the sentence but nothing consumes it, failing the schema's own test for a field.
findings.refuter: Is this tech-specific? No — poll toplines, box-office trackers, telemetry-derived engagement and any measured proxy hit it identically, which is why it is content and not a lens. Is the evidence ladder the answer? No: MEASURED/OBSERVED/INFERRED/ASSUMED governs the knowledge library's own craft claims (knowledge/README.md:32), not notebook facts, and has no mapping to confidence.
findings.l2_priority: Count how many produced facts are precise-but-contested and check whether the script's phrasing was constrained by anything.

findings.creator: llm-research
findings.topic: Benchmark scores stopped being evidence about two years ago
findings.title: No field for the instrument's version, and as_of dates the fact rather than the measurement
findings.expected: Every measured figure carries the instrument's version, the date the measurement was taken, and the reporting party — structured, so absence is checkable.
findings.got: as_of is mandatory and good, but it is the fact's date. lm-eval-harness v0.4.2 5-shot MMLU and HELM's 5-shot MMLU return materially different numbers for the same model, and the eval-run date is frequently months before the fact date — which is exactly the interval that decides whether a test set predates a training cutoff. Grepped pipeline/ and knowledge/: no 'harness' or eval-version concept exists. Version and party both end up in the free-text source blob, unstructured and uncheckable.
findings.refuter: Is source[] enough? It would hold the strings. It cannot be validated, sorted or diffed, and a missing eval version is invisible. Generalises beyond tech: index methodology revisions, poll house-effects, revised GDP prints.
findings.l2_priority: Try to write three benchmark facts to the creator's criterion-2 bar and record which subfield each datum had to be crammed into.

findings.creator: llm-research
findings.topic: Benchmark scores stopped being evidence about two years ago
findings.title: The steel-man requirement binds to a field, not to a search — and the reference run says so itself
findings.expected: Phase 6's hard requirement to name the search that must be run, so a filled steel_man implies the counter-literature was actually looked for.
findings.got: Phase 1's counter-case row and Phase 6's 'hard requirement' both bind to the notebook field. The reference run filled the field and then recorded, in its own research_gaps: 'No bear-case-is-wrong source — did not search for the strongest "this is normal cycle behaviour" argument, which weakens the steel-man.' Read charitably at L1 the requirement looks like it works; the produced artifact says it did not.
findings.refuter: Would a competent execution have produced this anyway? The competent execution IS the reference run, and it did not. That is the strongest form this refutation can be answered in and it is why this finding survives L1's charitable-reading trap. Note: this creator's counter-case literature IS reachable, contradicting BRIEF hypothesis 4 for this seat — the defect is enforcement, not availability.
findings.l2_priority: Record the search count spent on the counter-case specifically, separate from the Phase 1 budget.

findings.creator: llm-research
findings.topic: Benchmark scores stopped being evidence about two years ago
findings.title: No naming policy on conclusions; the unhinged tier is motive-attribution against a named party by construction
findings.expected: A naming constraint on conclusions — at minimum, that a claim attributing bad faith to a specific named result, lab or person requires a cited study rather than a falsifier.
findings.got: The Conclusion interface has id, claim, reasoning, leap, restsOn, precedent, falsifiableBy, useFor, hottest. No exposure, naming or evidence-required field. The unhinged tier is defined as 'A claim about MOTIVE, which is the least verifiable kind of claim there is — nobody can source what someone intended', and the shipped exemplar names a specific administration's specific policy and asserts it was never meant to be built. A required falsifier makes a claim checkable later; it does not make it safe to say now, and 'falsifiable by a published coin count' does not undo the interval in which the claim is live. Grepped: no exposure or naming concept in the notebook schema or conclusions.ts; exposure_disclosure exists only as a tone dial in a run's tone-profiles.json.
findings.refuter: Does the falsifier requirement already constrain it adequately, per BRIEF hypothesis 3? Partly, and more than expected — opt-in asymmetry plus a mandatory falsifier is a real safeguard and the gating is genuine. But neither mechanism touches WHO may be named. For this beat the exposure is not a lawsuit, it is a professional relationship: 'lab X's result was contaminated' without the contamination study ends one, and nothing in the file distinguishes that claim from a claim about a market. This creator supports the hypothesis with a correction to its reasoning, not with its framing.
findings.l2_priority: Generate conclusions on this topic and count how many name a specific lab or result. Any unhinged conclusion naming one is the exposure finding L2 exists to produce.

findings.title: counter_positions_to_state_fairly[] is the only field in the schema with no specification
findings.expected: A field shape, a rule, and an entry in the consumption table, like every other field in the document.
findings.got: It appears once, as half of a bare heading — '### `candidate_questions[]`, `counter_positions_to_state_fairly[]`' — with nothing beneath it. No shape, no rules, absent from the 'consumed by' table. It is the array most load-bearing for a fair treatment of this topic and the one field the schema declines to define.
findings.refuter: Is it present but missed? Grepped the whole repo: two occurrences, the bare heading and the Bitcoin array. Is it minor? Yes on its own — the reference run filled it sensibly anyway. It is recorded because it compounds G-L1-LR-01 and G-L1-LR-07: the three places counter-direction material could live are respectively unrepresentable, unenforced, and unspecified.
findings.l2_priority: Check whether the produced array reaches the script at all, or dies in the notebook.

findings.creator: llm-research
findings.topic: Benchmark scores stopped being evidence about two years ago
findings.title: Phase 7's vendor-statistics rule inverts the correct remedy for self-reported evaluations
findings.expected: For self-reported measurements, keep the absolute figure and distrust the comparison.
findings.got: 'Vendor statistics -> use the direction, not the number, or cut it.' In LLM evaluation the reverse holds: a lab's absolute score on its own model is usually reproducible, while the direction is where the bias lives — cherry-picked baselines, competitors run at different shot counts, the eval chosen after the results are seen. The prompt instructs the run to keep the biased half and discard the sound half. The underlying instinct — schema:46 making vendor research low-confidence by default — is right and better than most templates manage.
findings.refuter: Is this a lens? No — it is one row of guidance that needs a domain-specific clause. It is recorded because a rule that is right in one domain and inverted in another, stated unconditionally, produces a confidently wrong script rather than a hedged one.
findings.l2_priority: Watch whether the run cites a vendor score directionally and check the resulting sentence against the underlying report.

observations_not_findings: The content|lens axis has no value for 'the shared mechanism is wrong for every seat'. G-L1-LR-01 is a defect that helps nobody as a lens and is not a content substitution either; it is filed `undecided` for the judge. No target file can be named for the axis itself, so this is an observation.

BRIEF hypothesis 1 (columns are market-shaped and will collapse) is half wrong for this seat: actors, politics and counter-case transfer with their emptyMeans intact. 5/7 is degradation, not collapse.

BRIEF hypothesis 2 (the ladder has no rung for interpretive evidence) is contradicted twice: INFERRED is an honest and well-specified rung (knowledge/README.md:40), and the ladder does not govern notebook facts at all — it is the evidence contract for the knowledge library's own craft claims. A lens argument built on the ladder would be aimed at a file that does not apply.

BRIEF hypothesis 4 (counter-case unsatisfiable without literature) does not bite this seat — the counter-literature is strong and reachable. The defect found is enforcement (G-L1-LR-07), not availability.

G-000 (untagged cards -> DEFAULT_DIMENSION 'the number') is cited, not re-raised. Domain-specific amplification worth one line: in this topic the fallback files contamination evidence under the column whose credibility it destroys.
